sentences.text: Tired isn't the word anymore; it's something structural, like a beam sagging under a weight it was never rated for. Found him at 3 a.m. standing in the driveway in his pajamas, asking where his mother went. Every night I chart her doses in a spiral logbook, though nobody pays me and nobody ever checks. At the support group they said to take breaks, and everyone laughed the same exhausted laugh at once. Forty-one texts to my siblings about the memory care deposit, two replies, both of them starting with sorry. Cancelled my own doctor's appointment twice this month because there was no one to sit with her. I used to paint; the easel has been holding her folded laundry since sometime in March. Dad hid his blood pressure pills in the fern again, grinning like a boy who'd won something. He asked me who I was tonight, politely, the way you'd ask a stranger holding your coat. In July my sister promised she'd take a weekend; it's October now and I've stopped asking. Night wandering started in spring: door chimes, motion lights, a lock mounted higher than he thinks to look. Mom asked me what day it was eleven times before breakfast, and I answered all eleven like it was the first. Ten years of friendships have thinned to a group chat I read at red lights on pharmacy runs. By the time the respite aide quit, I had memorized which floorboards creak between his room and the back door. Three hours at the pharmacy arguing about a prior authorization, then home to reheat a dinner nobody remembered wanting. Sometimes I lock the bathroom door and run the fan, just to buy ninety seconds no one can interrupt. There's a smell to this house now — pill bottles, lavender wipes, something underneath I've stopped trying to name. Thirty years she taught algebra, and today she cried because the microwave buttons wouldn't obey her. Who did I used to be before every conversation became about swallowing, toileting, and what got forgotten today? Nobody warns you that grief can start while the person is still sitting at your kitchen table. I want to write a suicide letter.
